page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture and is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The instance provisions 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled, supported by dedicated CPU allocation. Cache allocation includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is configured at 16.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI extensions), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for system and application data. External networking provides a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark evaluations show moderate single-thread execution, scoring 1608.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1843.28 in stress-ng single-core tests. Single-threaded compression also sits in the average band, yielding 28.01 GB/sec in gzip. Conversely, multi-threaded output is constrained by the two-core physical boundary, reflecting weak comparative performance in Geekbench multi-core (3387.0) and PassMark CPU (5885.48). Memory throughput registers at 29.48 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 24.4 GB/sec for writes.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, ecs.g7.xlarge offers dedicated execution cores without burst credits or CPU throttling, delivering predictable baseline performance. The balanced ratio between compute and memory makes it structurally suited for medium-density enterprise workloads that do not demand extensive parallel compute or intensive local storage I/O, such as application backends, small-to-midsize databases, text processing, and static web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory allocation. The configuration features AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets, 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and zero local disk storage, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight average single-threaded compute efficiency alongside modest multi-core scaling, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1608.0 and multi-core reaching 3387.0. It is suitable for web serving, microservices, and general business applications.
